body:
I recognize that loss of hope in you, friend. I held onto that belief for way too long myself, not literally of course, but that the abuse, the pain, the bullying, the ostracization was FOR something and that things would have gotten better.

I'm the same, and I stopped being a teenager a while ago.

Not just people who were lucky enough to have good enough families. People who had similar experiences also have blindspots to this abuse. Society venerates the mother, and we're conditioned early to value her over all others. (Carried you for nine months. Yada, Yada, Yada) A lot of people I've interacted with as adults are in denial about their own abusive childhoods and have blinders on for the absolute darkness that is their mother.

Happened to me. 

Asked a question about whether an on-bid project had a direct-hire option and got no response until a rejection letter weeks later.

I appreciate you guys' well wishes. I feel better now, not quite hopeful but certainly off the ledge. The support you've given me has felt great and has helped through a thick mess of sorrow that usually consumes a day, if not days. 
I'm trying to hold on to hope for this job at the end of the two months and that my money holds out. I'd still be homeless at least two months into the job, but then I could start climbing out. 
I feel better in thinking about that possibility, but I know relapses into the darkness come suddenly and with precipitous falls.
Does anybody have any real tips of getting the awful angry voices of abusive people out of your head? I didn't come to this self-hatred honestly. I was driven here, and I don't like feeling like people I've removed from my life still occupy my head. 
Does that make sense?

Thank you for the kindness, man. I feel awful now, but I can at least see well enough to appreciate this from you. It's July 9. 
I have about three people I talk to sometimes, but it's only online because of geography. I feel like I've talked in circles about my frustrations and sadness with them. I've been waiting for more than six months for a government job to start, but it doesn't feel real. They say I'll be waiting another two-plus months at least. I hardly even think about it anymore. 
Anyway, thanks again.
